name: STÝRIVOLT
description: Stýrivolt is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from the Faroe Islands, belonging to the Karnöffel group. A 48-card pack is used (tens removed from a standard French deck). Each player receives 9 cards in batches of three; 12 cards remain as stock. The dealer determines two chosen suits from the stock; cards in those suits have special powers (stikkar, lambs, taking cards). There is no requirement to follow suit. The team that wins at least five of the nine tricks wins the hand. Winning the first five tricks (vol) scores a bonus.

content.text: Stýrivolt is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from the Faroe Islands, belonging to the Karnöffel group. A 48-card pack is used (tens removed from a standard French deck). Each player receives 9 cards in batches of three; 12 cards remain as stock. The dealer determines two chosen suits from the stock; cards in those suits have special powers (stikkar, lambs, taking cards). There is no requirement to follow suit. The team that wins at least five of the nine tricks wins the hand. Winning the first five tricks (vol) scores a bonus.

Stýrivolt descends from the German game Karnöffel and probably evolved in the early 17th century, spreading to Scandinavia; the name stýr-wålt appears in Sweden in 1658 (Georg Stiernhielm's poem Hercules). It has been played on the Faroe Islands since the 18th century and is documented in Jens Christian Svabo's travel writings (1781–1782) and in Danish game compendia from 1774 onward. The game survived as a Faroese tradition while largely disappearing from Denmark; rules were recorded in the cultural magazine Varðin (1975) and in later English-language rule publications.
Deal 9 cards to each player, 3 at a time. Twelve cards remain as stock; the dealer uses them to determine the two chosen suits.

items.text: Cutting for a stikkar: Cards are cut before the deal; the cutter may look at the bottom card of the stock. If it is a permanent stikkar, it is exposed and can be exchanged by the holder of the king of that suit before the first trick.
Choosing suits face up: As the dealer chooses suits, the cards turned from the stock are laid face up so everyone can see them.
Play with compulsory beating: Every player must beat the highest card so far played to the trick if possible, unless that card was played by their partner.
